title: Level 4 (Expert) - C-23
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 6NT. It appears, on general principles, that it is right to duck this trick. West will not continue diamonds. He will switch and South's early duck will put the contract in danger when the heart finesse was working.

South will continue by unblocking in spades and running the clubs (it does not matter if the ♦A is cashed first). On the play of dummy's last winner, East easily can let go a diamond, but South is squeezed. Discarding the ♦A leaves South with a heart loser. Discarding the ♥2 blocks the heart suit. Discarding the ♥Q or ♥J allows East to build a heart trick by covering with the ♥K when the ♥10 is led.

South's duck "on general principles" at trick 1 was wrong. The contract depends strictly on the heart finesse. By ducking at trick 1, South is rectifying the count for a one-suit squeeze against himself. The hand plays very simply if the ♦A is won at trick 1.

South unblocks the spades as before and runs the clubs. On the play of the ♠Q, South can painlessly discard the ♦J. The ♥10 is played next. Whether or not East plays the ♥K, South will lose only 1 trick at the end.
